open.speaker: tn_volunteer
lines: tn_volunteer
Everything on the rail's a pound, books are twenty pence, tapes are ten and I'll not haggle, the Lifeboat needs it more than you do. I'm Pat.
tn_volunteer
If you're after the box of cassettes, somebody's been through it already this week. Left it tidy. Nobody leaves it tidy.
june
A tidy box. Whoever was in before us knew which tape they wanted and put the rest back in order.

passives.line: There's a stack of things behind the counter, priced and never put on the floor. She's labelled them because that's the job. She can't sell them.
The dummy on the high shelf has its head turned to the door. When you came in it was facing the room. You think.

options.text: Ten pence a tape is a bargain, Pat. We'll not haggle. Mind if we ask about the box?
We'll haggle for the Lifeboat's sake, then. Call it fifteen.
Who went through the box? We'll need a name.

jigsaw.speaker: tn_volunteer
lines: tn_volunteer
You can ask. I'm doing the jigsaws, they've all got a piece missing and it's always the sky, I don't know why it's always the sky.

haggle.speaker: tn_volunteer
lines: tn_volunteer
...Fifteen. Go on. You're the first in twenty years to haggle up. Sit on the stool, it only wobbles the one way.

name.speaker: tn_volunteer
lines: tn_volunteer
You'll need a name. I'll need a receipt from the Pope. It's a charity shop, love, I don't sign them in. A woman. Good coat. Didn't buy.
miriam
A charity shop volunteer with a wobbly stool, and we asked her for a name like she's a desk sergeant.

hub.speaker: tn_volunteer
lines: tn_volunteer
Tuesdays and Thursdays, me. Mondays it's Jean and she'd tell you nothing because she knows nothing, so you've picked your day.
hub.prompt: Pat prices a jigsaw and doesn't look up.

options.text: The things behind the counter. They're priced. You've not put them out.

fail.line: Those are waiting for a shelf. Everything's waiting for a shelf. Have a look at the books.

options.text: Dyer and Dennis, thirty years on the pier. Was he on the bill in '73?
The dummy's turned round since we came in. You've seen it move. You've told somebody.
We bought the tape. We'd like to tell you what's on it before anyone else does.

static.line: The dummy's mouth is open a quarter inch. It wasn't. Don't price the tapes. Ask her who she's been talking to after closing.

behind.speaker: tn_volunteer
lines: tn_volunteer
...Dennis. The dummy. And a scrapbook of the act, and a hat with a bell on. His sister said sell the lot.
tn_volunteer
I've priced it. I can't put him on the floor with the Tupperware.
tn_volunteer
He's not creepy. People say they're creepy. He's got a kind face. It's just that his face is the only one left of Mr Dyer and I'd be selling it for a pound.
elijah
She's priced a dead man's face and can't let it go. That's not superstition. That's a wake nobody held.

pier73.speaker: tn_volunteer
lines: tn_volunteer
He was. Twice daily, and that summer the camp borrowed him. Sent a tall one up to him for lessons in the voice, the no-breath voice, four afternoons in the Pavilion.
tn_volunteer
He came back off the fourth afternoon and wouldn't do the children's matinee for a month. Said the lad learned it too fast. Said he learned it like he'd already known it.
june
Four afternoons to learn a technique that takes years. Either he was a natural, or he wasn't learning. He was being checked.

pier73_fail.speaker: tn_volunteer
lines: tn_volunteer
'73? Love, I was in Southampton with my first husband in '73 and I'd not have remembered the pier if it had fallen in.
tn_volunteer
Ask the Professor. The Punch man. He knows every act since the war.
teddy
The Punch man. A ventriloquist's voice, and a Punch and Judy man who'd know how it's done. That's the pier, next.

dennis.speaker: tn_volunteer
lines: tn_volunteer
...I turn him to the wall when I lock up. Every night since March. And every morning he's facing the door, and the shutter's down, and I've got the only key.
tn_volunteer
I told the vicar. He came and stood in here and said a thing over him, and Dennis faced the wall for a week, and then he didn't. The vicar said he'd come back. He hasn't.
tn_volunteer
I don't think it's Mr Dyer. I'd not mind if it was Mr Dyer. I think it's something that's learned the trick of him.
vera
A dead man's voice on the tape, a dead man's face on the shelf, and something practising both. It is learning a part.

dennis_fail.speaker: tn_volunteer
lines: tn_volunteer
Ha! Move! He's wood, love. It's a shop. Things get knocked. Jean knocks everything.
tn_volunteer
...That'll be fifteen for the tapes, since you said. Mind the stool.
ruth
That laugh was a door shutting, dear. She's seen it. She'll say it to the vicar before she says it to us.

tape.speaker: tn_volunteer
lines: tn_volunteer
The rhymes. It'll be the rhymes, he always did the rhymes to warm up. 'Hickory dickory.' Without his chest moving. Used to frighten the Brownies silly.
tn_volunteer
Put it back in the box when you're done with it. His sister might want it one day, and I'd like to be able to say it's here.
june
She told us what's on it before we could. She's heard it. She listened to that tape alone in here, after hours, and she's still opening up on Tuesdays.
